subject: SapphirePay — sudden throughput drop and answer coherence decline after model upgrade
messages:
From: Ethan Shaw <ethan.shaw@sapphirepay.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jordan Price <jordan.price@sapphirepay.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SapphirePay: sudden throughput drop & answer coherence regressions after v5.2/int8 rollout

Hi Karthik,

We started seeing a sharp throughput drop this morning (≈40% fewer requests processed per minute) and a rise in error rates (HTTP 500 / decode stalls) following the rolling update you pushed for our production slot (v5.2 + int8 qprofile). In addition a subset of end-user flows are returning incoherent answers — wrong merchant IDs and duplicated fields in structured outputs.

This is impacting payment authorization at peak times; we had to throttle a couple of hotspots which is now creating backpressure for our downstream reconciler. I attached a short sample from the logs and a screenshot from our tracing dashboard.

Can we get an immediate rollback or a mitigation plan? We’re flagged for an exec review if this continues into the afternoon.

What's urgent for us:
- ETA for rollback to prior model/quant profile or a safe canary flip.
- Temporary QOS/ingress suggestions so we can avoid failed transactions during peak windows.
- Confirmation whether this is a model accuracy regression vs runtime decode issue.

Thanks,
Ethan
Ethan Shaw
Head of SRE, SapphirePay
E: ethan.shaw@sapphirepay.com
A: Attachment: sapphire_error_sample.log (text, 45KB); sapphire_topology_trace.png (png, 230KB)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ethan Shaw <ethan.shaw@sapphirepay.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2027 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SapphirePay: sudden throughput drop & answer coherence regressions after v5.2/int8 rollout

Ethan — thanks for the heads up and for the attached samples. We’re looking at this as P1.

Quick notes from triage so far (internal kernel + ops):
- The rollout you referenced used the new int8 qprofile (q_v3) plus the v5.2 parameter set. Runtime metrics show increased KV cache misses on long-sequence payment flows which is consistent with extra decode work.
- Error patterns (decode stalls followed by 500s) line up with a scheduler congestion scenario under our continuous-batching heuristics when sequences hit worst-case token lengths.

Immediate actions we propose:
1) Temporary rate limit of non-critical flows (customer support chat, enrichment paths) — we can push a route-level throttle from our control plane within 10 minutes if you approve.
2) Emergency canary: revert 10% of prod traffic back to q_v2/int16 variant — this is low-risk and we can observe latency/quality delta.
3) If canary looks good, escalate to a full rollback of the quant profile across your reserved pool.

I’ll coordinate with operations right now and can host an emergency bridge in ~20 minutes. Lauren and Rishi are looped for exec comms and runbook execution.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: SapphirePay: sudden throughput drop & answer coherence regressions after v5.2/int8 rollout

Karthik / Rishi — quick internal note before the bridge:
- Financial impact: customer reports authorization delays affecting peak batches (East coast morning). This will escalate to commercial if not resolved in 2–3 hours.
- Ask: Prepare a short executive summary for the CRO/COO (1 slide) and get a clear recommended action (rollback vs canary expansion). If we can present a low-risk rollback that re-establishes throughput and accuracy, we should prioritize that.
- Ops: please document the exact traffic slice, the model variant IDs, and the qprofile hash so Legal / Finance can include in a remediation agreement if SLA credits are requested.

I’m ready to join the exec bridge; looping Tessa for postmortem facilitation.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
VP, Customer Success Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Maria Vega <maria.vega@sapphirepay.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ethan Shaw <ethan.shaw@sapphirepay.com>, Jordan Price <jordan.price@sapphirepay.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SapphirePay: sudden throughput drop & answer coherence regressions after v5.2/int8 rollout

Thanks for the quick response. A few clarifications:
- The issue started right after the 02:00 UTC maintenance window when you promoted v5.2/int8. We have temporarily rerouted high-value payments to a fallback path but it increases latency for users.
- Attached are two traces and a short sample of malformed structured outputs coming from our production environment. You can see duplicate merchant_id fields in the JSON payloads — this is _not_ acceptable for reconciliation.

We will require:
1) A concrete timeline for rollback if you recommend it.
2) A proposed ETA for a permanent fix (if this is model-level) and communication we can provide to our ops leadership.
3) Confirmation about whether you will provide SLA credits for failed authorizations while rollout was active (we have contractual thresholds).

Please advise on the bridge time.

Regards,
Maria Vega
VP, Platform Engineering, SapphirePay
A: Attachment: sapphire_error_sample.log; sapphire_topology_trace.png

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Vega <maria.vega@sapphirepay.com>, Ethan Shaw <ethan.shaw@sapphirepay.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2027 11:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SapphirePay: sudden throughput drop & answer coherence regressions after v5.2/int8 rollout

Maria — after consulting ops and runtime engineering, recommendation and action plan below:

Recommended immediate action (P0):
- Emergency canary flip: divert 15% of your production traffic to the previous quant profile (q_v2/int16) and v5.1 variant now. This is non-disruptive and will give us a direct comparator for both throughput and answer coherence within 15 minutes.
- If the canary restores throughput and structured output correctness, we will proceed with a full rollback of the qprofile across your reserved pool. Estimated rollback time: 30–45 minutes from approval.

Mitigations we will apply in parallel:
- Tighten continuous-batching thresholds for long sequences in your tenant to reduce KV cache churn.
- Temporary route-level rate limits for enrichment/chat flows that are non-blocking for authorizations (we will not throttle authorization routes).
- Capture extended traces and a prioritized request sample set; ops will push a zip to the shared drive for joint debugging.

Commercial / SLA: Rishi (cc) will lead the SLA credit conversation; we will preserve all telemetry and logs for a postmortem.

Bridge: target 11:30 AM PT for a 30-minute bridge (I will host). Please confirm you can join.

Approval to proceed with the canary/rollback required from Maria or a named delegate.

-Karthik

Maria / Ethan — I’m stepping in to coordinate this at the executive level.

Commitments:
- We will execute the emergency canary now and apply a rollback to q_v2/int16 across your reserved pool if the canary indicates restoration of throughput/quality. Target full rollback completion within 45 minutes of canary approval.
- Redwood will preserve all logs and provide a draft postmortem and remediation plan within 48 hours. Tessa will run the postmortem and produce an action list with owners.
- Regarding SLA credits: we will analyze tokenized failed authorizations during the affected window and engage finance/legal to prepare a credit proposal within 24 hours. The commercial team will coordinate directly with your procurement contact.

Bridge: I will host a CTO/CRO bridging call at 16:00 PT — invite to follow. We will include a 1-slide exec summary and timeline for rollback + follow-up.

Apologies for the disruption; we will treat this as a top-priority incident until resolved.

-Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
VP, Global Customer Success
Redwood Inference
